role: The abstract server base: the run loop, the per-tick driver over the three worlds, the config manager and network system wiring, and the server-property state. The integrated server in the oracle subclasses it and the lockstep replaces its wall-clock loop.
scope_reason: The integrated server is the game's server; the oracle pins its loop (Lockstep.server, one tick per client tick) and the native replay reproduces the same tick sequence. Nothing in world.conf switches any of it. Deferred: native never writes save files; Java writes every checkpoint (product decision, not a gap for the GPU or the golden chain); status response and wall-clock scaffolding are outside the tick (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md).

notes: The tick loop's game content is proven per tick by test_servertick.c against the oracle's ServerTickProbe recordings (out/java/servertick/s1, s42): every WorldServer.tick write row, spawn row and scalar. world-daynight-s1 and world-storm-s1 cover the weather and daylight timers tick() drives; nether-trip-s1 covers worldServerForDimension's other two worlds. The abstract getters are n/a because the integrated server's answers are constants the replay carries (difficulty through surv_world_setup, game type survival, structures off). Closed by lane/idxworld: updateTimeLightAndEntities' S03 to each world's players every 20th getTickCounter (the overworld's time before its tick; after it for a Nether or End player) is ported (session.c session_row) and held at every frame by idx-clientview-s1's client clock. The status response (field_147147_p's refresh, the player sample's field_147146_q shuffle, the icon) answers a server list ping, which a single-player world never gets; the wall-clock loop scaffolding (getSystemTimeMillis, tickTimeArray, the can't-keep-up warning) is what the lockstep replaces; sendPlayerInfoToAllPlayers' S38 feeds the tab list, which the single-player client never shows (GuiPlayerTabOverlay needs a remote server or a second player). The disk half is n/a (lane/idxworld): every save this game makes is the oracle's (a checkpoint's save, session.sh's Save and Quit through Java: AGENTS.md 'Playing a full game'), and the native engine reads what it wrote (region.c for the overworld's region files, the snapshot's saved chunks for DIM-1 and DIM1, structures.json, villages.nbt, worldinfo.nbt, player_server.nbt); writing those files natively is the deferred product work of the 2026-09-25 triage (SPEC.md NEXT, '11 deferred save-writing'; out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md, 'Deferred, not noise'). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings).
